transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see us today?
I feel like I’ve been stuck in this low, heavy mood for years and I just don’t enjoy anything the way I used to. It just feels like there's this constant weight on me that I can't seem to shake off.
Can you tell me more about when you first started feeling this way, was it a gradual change or did it start after a specific event, and how long have you been experiencing this low mood?

It started gradually a little over two years ago, rather than all at once. It really began when I took on a much heavier caseload at work and started driving down to care for my mother on weekends. Over time, those responsibilities just slowly wore me down, and this heavy mood settled in.

You mentioned that your heavy mood started around the time you took on more work and began caring for your mother, but have you experienced any significant improvements in your mood during periods when those responsibilities were temporarily reduced or absent?

No, not at all. Even on the rare weekends when I don't have to travel or when work slows down a bit, that gray feeling is still right there. It has been completely constant for the last two years without any real breaks or moments where I felt like my old self.

Have you experienced any periods of significant improvement in your mood or functioning that lasted for at least two months since this low mood started, or has it been consistently present over the past two years?

No, I haven't had any breaks or periods of improvement that lasted anywhere near two months. It has just been a continuous, daily struggle since I took on the extra work and caregiving. I haven't felt like my old self at all during this whole time.

Have you experienced any episodes of significantly elevated mood, increased energy, or decreased need for sleep that lasted for several days or more at any point in your life, including before this two-year period of low mood began?

No, I’ve never experienced anything like that. My energy has never been abnormally high, and I've never had periods where I didn't need sleep or felt unusually elevated. My mood has generally just been either normal or low and heavy like it is now.
Can you think of any times during the past two years when your low mood has worsened or improved slightly, even if briefly, in response to specific events, seasons, or personal circumstances?

To be honest, I haven't really noticed any ups or downs like that. This low, heavy feeling has just been a constant, steady baseline for me over the last couple of years without any real breaks or improvements.
You mentioned not enjoying things the way you used to, can you tell me more about what specific activities or hobbies you've lost interest in over the past two years?

I used to love painting, hiking, and going to museums or senior-center workshops with my friends. Now, I've stopped doing all of those things and find myself turning down invitations because I just don't have the energy or motivation anymore. It feels like I'm just dragging myself through the days instead of living.

Have you experienced any periods where your low mood was significantly worse for a shorter period, say a few weeks or a couple of months, followed by a return to your current baseline level of low mood?

No, I haven't really noticed any times where it got much worse for a few weeks and then went back to normal. It has just been a steady, constant, heavy baseline of low mood that has stayed with me continuously for the last two-plus years.

Can you describe any differences in how you experience your low mood, such as changes in appetite, sleep patterns, or concentration, that might help distinguish between periods of worse or better mood, even if those periods are not significantly different from your baseline?

Yes, my sleep and appetite have definitely changed. I struggle to fall asleep with my mind racing, then wake up around 3 or 4 in the morning unable to drift back off, which leaves me completely exhausted. I also have no appetite, often skipping lunch at work and just picking at crackers or cereal for dinner, so my clothes have started hanging looser on me.
Do you often feel guilty or worthless, or have recurring thoughts that you're a burden to others, and if so, how frequently do these feelings occur?

No, I don't really feel guilty or worthless, and I've never felt like I'm a burden to others. Those specific feelings haven't really been a part of what I've been experiencing. It is more just this constant, heavy cloud and exhaustion.

You've described a continuous low mood for over two years without significant improvements, but can you recall if there have been any subtle variations in the intensity of your symptoms over time, even if the overall low mood has remained constant?

No, it has really felt very constant and steady without any noticeable variations. It's hard to recall any lighter periods or times when the weight lifted even a little bit since this all started. It has just been the same heavy feeling day in and day out.

Can you confirm if you have experienced any distinct episodes of depression that lasted for more than two weeks but less than two years, which could help differentiate between persistent and episodic patterns of depression?

No, I haven't had any distinct episodes that come and go like that. It has just been one steady, continuous low mood for a little over two years, ever since I took on the extra caregiving and work responsibilities. It has really felt like a constant, unbroken cloud hanging over me the entire time.

You mentioned losing interest in activities like painting and hiking, can you tell me if there are any activities or things that still bring you some joy or pleasure, even if it's not as much as before?

Honestly, nothing really seems to bring me joy or pleasure anymore. Even when I try to do things, they just feel like a chore or leave me feeling flat and empty, so I can't really think of anything that still gives me that spark.

Have you ever had a period in your life before these past two years where you felt completely normal and without any significant low mood for an extended time, or has this low mood been a recurring issue throughout your adult life?

Yes, before these past two or three years, I felt completely normal and had a lot of energy and enthusiasm for my life, including my art, hiking, and volunteering. This low, heavy mood is a completely new experience for me that only started when my work stress and caregiving duties for my mother piled up.

Can you think of any time before the last two years when you experienced a period of low mood that lasted for more than two weeks, or has this been the first and only continuous episode of low mood you've experienced?

Yes, this is the first and only time in my life I have ever experienced a low mood like this. Before it started about two or three years ago when my work and caregiving duties got so heavy, I felt very balanced and active, and I truly enjoyed my hobbies like hiking and art.

You've mentioned that this low mood started around two to three years ago and has been constant since, but can you think of any factors or events that might have triggered the onset of this mood, or was it more of a gradual accumulation of stressors?

It was really a combination of both. It started about three years ago when my agency lost senior aides and I had to take on a much heavier caseload, right as my mother's health declined and I began traveling on weekends to care for her. Over the next two years, those initial triggers turned into a gradual, exhausting pile of stress that slowly wore me down.

Have you ever had a period of at least two months where you felt significantly better, almost back to your normal self, since this low mood started, or has it been a continuous, unbroken period of low mood?

No, it has been a completely continuous, unbroken period of low mood since it started. I haven't had any times—not even for a couple of weeks, let alone two months—where I felt back to my normal self. It has just been a steady, heavy feeling hanging over me the entire time.

Can you confirm whether you have experienced any periods of significant depressive symptoms that lasted for less than two years, which could help differentiate between persistent and episodic depression?

No, I haven't had any shorter phases of depression like that. This low, heavy feeling has been completely constant and steady for over two years, ever since I took on the extra work and started caring for my mom. It has just been one long, unbroken period rather than something that comes and goes.

You've described a constant low mood for over two years without significant improvements, can you help me understand if you've ever had periods where your symptoms met the full criteria for a major depressive episode, such as having at least five specific depressive symptoms for at least two weeks, within this broader period of low mood?

I'm not really sure about those specific medical criteria or if I've had a distinct, worse period with five specific symptoms like that. It has mostly just felt like a steady, continuous heavy weight rather than coming in clear, separate waves.

Can you clarify if there have been any periods, even brief, where you felt like you were at the lowest point or had the most severe symptoms, which might indicate a major depressive episode within this ongoing low mood?

I haven't really noticed any specific periods where it suddenly got much worse or where I hit a distinct lowest point. Instead, it has just felt like a steady, continuous, and heavy low mood that has remained at the same draining level for the past two years.

Can you confirm if this current episode of low mood is the only one you've experienced in your lifetime, or have you had previous episodes of depression that resolved before this two-year period began?
Yes, this is definitely the first time I've gone through something like this. I don't recall ever experiencing a low mood like this before this current period started.

Given that you've had this continuous low mood for over two years without significant improvement, can you think of any periods within this time where you might have met the criteria for a major depressive episode, such as having at least five depressive symptoms like persistent sadness, loss of interest, changes in appetite or sleep, fatigue, feelings of worthlessness, or recurrent thoughts of death, for at least two weeks?

I haven't really had any distinct periods where things got suddenly much worse, and I've never experienced thoughts of death or worthlessness. Instead, it has just been a steady, continuous baseline of low mood, fatigue, poor sleep, and low appetite for the entire two-plus years.

Considering your symptoms have been constant for over two years, can you think of any subtle differences in how you've experienced your low mood, such as variations in energy levels or motivation, that might suggest periods where your symptoms were slightly more or less severe?

No, my low mood and lack of energy have been very steady and constant over the last two years, with no real periods where things felt lighter. While some days are physically more exhausting due to my caregiving demands, that underlying gray mood has remained a constant presence. I really haven't noticed any fluctuations or times of relief.
You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, can you think of any small things or everyday activities that still give you some pleasure, even if it's minimal?

Honestly, I can't think of anything that still gives me pleasure. Everything feels like I'm just going through the motions under a gray film, and even things I used to love—like my art, hiking, or joking with my clients—don't bring me any real joy anymore.

Can you think of any periods, even brief, where your low mood might have briefly lifted or significantly worsened, which could help clarify if this is one long episode or if there have been fluctuations within this two-year period?

No, there really haven't been any periods where the mood lifted or felt normal again. It has just been a very steady, constant heavy feeling over the last two-plus years without any real breaks. It has just felt like one long, continuous struggle.

Considering your low mood has been constant for over two years, can you recall any instances or periods where you felt like you were at a particularly low point, or where specific depressive symptoms like changes in appetite, sleep, or energy were more pronounced, even if briefly?

No, there hasn't been a distinct lowest point or a time when things suddenly got much worse. Instead, it’s just been a steady, unrelenting heaviness every single day, where barely eating, waking up at 3 AM with a racing mind, and feeling exhausted by simple chores are just my constant reality. It doesn't come in waves; it has just been a continuous daily drag for the last two years.

Can you clarify if you believe your current low mood represents a single, long-lasting episode of depression or if you think there might have been shorter episodes of depression within this two-year period that you haven't clearly distinguished?

It definitely feels like one continuous, long-lasting heavy mood rather than separate episodes that come and go. It has just been this single, steady gray cloud hanging over me constantly for the past two-plus years. I haven't experienced any distinct phases or breaks in it at all.

Can you think of any factors or events that might have triggered the onset of this mood, and do you believe the low mood has remained constant or have there been any subtle variations in its intensity over the two-year period?

It started a little over two years ago when I took on a much heavier caseload at work and my mother's health began to decline, requiring me to manage her care on weekends. Since then, this low, heavy feeling has been very steady and constant, like a gray film over everything that just doesn't lift.

You've mentioned losing interest in activities you used to enjoy, but can you think of any small, everyday pleasures, like taking a warm bath, reading a book, or sipping a favorite coffee, that still bring you some joy or comfort, even if it's very minimal?

Honestly, even those small things don't bring me any comfort or joy anymore. Just trying to do them feels like way too much effort, and if I do try, I'm just going through the motions without feeling any real warmth or relief.

Have you ever experienced any periods where your low mood significantly improved for a few months before returning to your current state, or has it been a steady, continuous low mood without any breaks?

No, there haven't been any periods of improvement like that. Ever since I took on the extra workload and started caring for my mom over two years ago, it has been a steady, continuous low mood without any breaks. It just feels like a constant, heavy weight that never lifts.
